description: Original examples of therapist-delivered clinical interventions for professional discussion; not a protocol, directive, or evidence-of-efficacy ranking. Qualifications, medical safety, consent and formulation matter.

interventions.title: Collaborative anxiety formulation
interventions.try: In session, map the feared meaning, context, attention, responses and consequences of a real situation. Examine realistic danger and access needs before selecting a change.
interventions.measure: Review whether the explanation fits the person's experience and identifies workable choices.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided approach experiment
interventions.try: Assess actual risks and needed accommodations, negotiate a voluntary manageable experiment, coach during it and debrief predictions against what occurred.
interventions.measure: Track chosen participation and learning; do not treat anxiety reduction as the sole outcome.
interventions.scope: Clinician screens medical/safety issues; never remove necessary accommodations.

interventions.title: Clinical accommodation experiment
interventions.try: Jointly analyze which demands create barriers and which responses reflect fear. In session compare feasible access changes, enlist relevant partners with consent, and review impacts.
interventions.measure: Compare participation, effort and overload in equivalent situations with and without the support.

interventions.title: Behavioral activation with therapist formulation
interventions.try: Map mood, fatigue, overload, rewards and opportunity restrictions. Use a session to choose and troubleshoot accessible, meaningful activity experiments with the person.
interventions.measure: Compare personally meaningful engagement and feasibility over repeated opportunities.

interventions.title: Guided work on self-critical beliefs
interventions.try: Help the person examine a self-critical conclusion, evidence, life context and possible alternatives. Rehearse a personally credible response in session.
interventions.measure: Use individualized self-criticism ratings alongside functioning and personally valued action.

interventions.title: Relapse signature and coordinated response plan
interventions.try: Map the person's pattern of sleep, activation, mood and functioning across episodes; distinguish baseline variation and medication effects. Coordinate a response plan with the treating team.
interventions.measure: Track individualized early warning changes, plan use and functional stability.
interventions.scope: Requires appropriate coordination with prescribing care; never substitute for urgent mania, psychosis or safety assessment.

interventions.title: Therapist-facilitated family support planning
interventions.try: With consent, help the person and supporters define what changes should prompt contact, which help is welcome and who makes which decisions. Rehearse the plan together.
interventions.measure: Monitor whether helpful actions are available when needed while autonomy is respected.

interventions.title: Therapist-led worry differentiation
interventions.try: In session distinguish solvable problems, uncertain outcomes and unavoidable demands. Guide appropriate problem-solving and values-based uncertainty work rather than using one technique for everything.
interventions.measure: Track time lost to repetitive worry, problem actions completed and tolerable uncertainty.

interventions.title: Uncertainty tolerance rehearsal
interventions.try: Together choose a low-risk decision, assess the need for more information, guide one decision without repeated guarantees and process what the person learned.
interventions.measure: Compare decision participation and checking/reassurance burden across comparable choices.

interventions.title: Panic-cycle case formulation
interventions.try: Use an actual event to map sensation, interpretation, alarm, response and possible recurrence. Check medical and contextual explanations and identify a collaborative treatment focus.
interventions.measure: Ask how accurately the cycle captures episodes and whether the person can identify useful next steps.
interventions.scope: New, severe or changed symptoms need medically appropriate evaluation.

interventions.title: Clinician-supervised panic experiment
interventions.try: When medically appropriate, a qualified therapist formulates feared predictions, obtains consent, structures an exposure/response experiment and debriefs outcomes together.
interventions.measure: Track prediction learning and restored chosen participation, not induced symptoms for their own sake.
interventions.scope: Interoceptive exposure requires indicated medical screening and qualified supervision.

interventions.title: Therapist-led interpersonal rehearsal
interventions.try: Explore the real communication demand, then model and rehearse a chosen interaction in session. Give collaborative feedback and support culturally and neurodevelopmentally appropriate styles.
interventions.measure: Evaluate usable self-advocacy, choice and communication access instead of eye contact or conformity.

interventions.title: Social evaluation hypothesis test
interventions.try: Help the person formulate one fear of being judged; check actual discrimination or relationship danger. Design a consented experiment or role-play and compare prediction and observed outcomes.
interventions.measure: Measure personally meaningful engagement and accuracy of predictions in context.

interventions.title: Collaborative graded exposure treatment
interventions.try: A qualified therapist evaluates safety, consent and functional aims, develops a flexible hierarchy, guides graded approach and processes learning.
interventions.measure: Track voluntary participation and feared outcome learning alongside accommodations.
interventions.scope: No unsafe exposures or pressure to override consent/medical advice.

interventions.title: Specialist ERP formulation and practice
interventions.try: An OCD-qualified clinician differentiates obsessions, rituals, reassurance and necessary safety actions; agrees on exposure/response prevention targets, coaches practice and revisits effects.
interventions.measure: Monitor time or interference from compulsions and return to chosen life activities.
interventions.scope: Do not confuse legitimate safety, medical care, disability supports or eating care with rituals.

interventions.title: Family accommodation consultation
interventions.try: With consent, identify which reassurance patterns may unintentionally reinforce compulsions and which are genuine support needs. Co-design nonpunitive changes and rehearse responses with supporters.
interventions.measure: Track supporter confidence and whether useful assistance remains accessible.

interventions.title: Body-image meaning and checking formulation
interventions.try: Collaboratively explore appearance beliefs, mirror/photo checking, shame, social pressures and avoidance. Use a structured case formulation to select a treatment approach without debating actual appearance.
interventions.measure: Track distress and interference plus chosen social/work participation.

interventions.title: Trauma-informed stabilization and shared formulation
interventions.try: Assess readiness, current safety, dissociation, supports and goals. Collaboratively link triggers and responses while avoiding unnecessary trauma detail, and select an appropriate phase of care.
interventions.measure: Monitor perceived safety, choice, coping effectiveness and functional participation.
interventions.scope: Trauma-processing treatments require suitable qualification and informed consent.

interventions.title: Specialist trauma-focused therapy
interventions.try: A qualified therapist uses an evidence-based trauma-focused method with individualized pacing, consent, response monitoring and active reassessment of stability and goals.
interventions.measure: Use appropriate symptom and function measures plus the person's assessment of safety and benefit.
interventions.scope: Do not treat this prompt as a protocol for unsupervised trauma exposure.

interventions.title: Collaborative transition-focused problem solving
interventions.try: Structure sessions around what changed, controllable and uncontrollable demands, losses, supports and person-defined priorities. Rehearse communication and one feasible adjustment strategy.
interventions.measure: Track goal progress, role participation and felt agency during the transition.

interventions.title: Grief-focused therapeutic meaning work
interventions.try: With sensitivity to culture and relationship, help the person explore loss-related distress, changing roles, ongoing bonds and wishes for connection without prescribing a timetable.
interventions.measure: Review impairment, meaningful connection and personally valued adaptation rather than grief 'completion'.

interventions.title: Dissociation-focused grounding and continuity planning
interventions.try: A trained therapist assesses episodes and safety, identifies individualized early signs, practices consensual grounding or orientation methods in session and documents what helps or worsens functioning.
interventions.measure: Record orientation, participation, aftereffects and support needs across contexts.
interventions.scope: Avoid suggestive memory-recovery techniques or assuming one explanatory model.

interventions.title: Non-leading functional dissociation assessment
interventions.try: Use careful phenomenological questions and functional observation to distinguish experiences, triggers, memory problems and possible medical causes; coordinate indicated assessment.
interventions.measure: Track time lost, continuity of daily roles and changes reported in a neutral language.

interventions.title: Therapist-delivered interpersonal chain analysis
interventions.try: With a collaborative and nonjudgmental approach, review a difficult interpersonal event, vulnerabilities, cue, actions, consequences and alternatives, without assuming intent or blame.
interventions.measure: Monitor relationship functioning, repair choices and ability to apply an agreed skill.

interventions.title: Structured emotion-regulation skills therapy
interventions.try: In session teach, model and rehearse an indicated skill; help the person adapt it for sensory or access needs, troubleshoot obstacles and review use without punitive compliance targets.
interventions.measure: Measure function after difficult emotions, skill usefulness and chosen safety goals.

interventions.title: Longitudinal interpersonal pattern formulation
interventions.try: The therapist and person explore repeated relationship themes across settings and time, including contextual harms, strengths and alternative explanations. Revise the formulation collaboratively.
interventions.measure: Review valued relationships, self-understanding and functioning rather than an assumed personality label.

interventions.title: Collaborative coping and relapse-support planning
interventions.try: Assess immediate risks and strengths, discuss distressing experiences without confrontation, coordinate with psychiatric care and negotiate usable coping and help-seeking responses.
interventions.measure: Track distress, role functioning, adherence to chosen supports and ability to obtain timely care.
interventions.scope: Medication and acute risk decisions belong to qualified medical teams.

interventions.title: CBT-informed work with distressing experiences
interventions.try: A trained clinician collaboratively examines meaning, threat and coping around unusual experiences without forcing agreement about their cause. Test safer alternatives only when appropriate.
interventions.measure: Monitor distress, agency, sleep and daily participation; symptoms alone do not measure benefit.

interventions.title: Therapist-led executive-function design
interventions.try: Observe task demands and access barriers, co-design external structure, practice a realistic task sequence in session and iteratively adjust cues with the person's feedback.
interventions.measure: Measure initiation latency, completion with supports and cognitive effort.

interventions.title: In-session task initiation coaching
interventions.try: Rehearse identifying the smallest functional step, arranging materials, planning a restart cue and handling interruptions during an actual selected task.
interventions.measure: Track supported starting and restarting across real opportunities.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided sensory and demand assessment
interventions.try: Map sensory demands, unpredictability and communication access across contexts. Trial environmental changes collaboratively rather than imposing habituation or masking.
interventions.measure: Compare participation, aftereffects, recovery cost and the person's choice.

interventions.title: Affirming communication-access intervention
interventions.try: With the person, adjust communication methods and practice boundaries or support requests in session; include partners only with consent and avoid enforcing normative social behavior.
interventions.measure: Measure whether authentic communication, refusals and preferences are understood and respected.

interventions.title: Supported decision-making assessment and coaching
interventions.try: Assess which accessible information, response methods and trusted supports make choices possible. Rehearse presenting real options, checking understanding and respecting refusal.
interventions.measure: Track opportunities offered, preferences expressed and choices honored.
interventions.scope: Do not infer global capacity from speech or one response.

interventions.title: Clinician-guided adaptive support experiment
interventions.try: Observe a person-chosen daily task with consent, identify environmental or communication barriers, model aids/supports and review participation without equating assistance with failure.
interventions.measure: Compare role participation and needed support; monitor dignity and effort.

interventions.title: Caregiver-child functional consultation
interventions.try: Assess safety and context, collect descriptive before/behavior/after observations, and collaboratively coach caregivers in co-regulation, predictable routines and repair.
interventions.measure: Track frequency with context, child safety, caregiver consistency and improved function.
interventions.scope: Avoid coercion or interpreting all distress as willful misconduct.

interventions.title: In-session caregiver skill rehearsal
interventions.try: Model one specific validation, limit-setting or co-regulation response; rehearse it with the caregiver and help plan a feasible real-world context for trying it.
interventions.measure: Monitor caregiver response quality, child safety and opportunities for child communication.

interventions.title: Clinician-guided escalation chain and interruption
interventions.try: Review a recent escalation from context to body signs, threat meaning, available choices and consequences. Rehearse a preferred pause, boundary or recovery response in session.
interventions.measure: Track time to notice early cues, harm reduction and successful safe reconnection.

interventions.title: Motivational interviewing for ambivalence
interventions.try: The trained therapist elicits the person's values and concerns with a nonjudgmental stance, clarifies ambivalence and collaborates on harm-reduction or treatment goals without coercion.
interventions.measure: Record self-chosen goals, engagement and functional change.
interventions.scope: Withdrawal and overdose risks require appropriate medical assessment.

interventions.title: Relapse/return-to-use safety planning
interventions.try: Explore triggers, access, relationships and practical barriers; coordinate medications or specialty care as indicated, and rehearse a nonpunitive re-entry plan after a setback.
interventions.measure: Monitor risk reduction, timely access to services and personally meaningful functioning.
interventions.scope: Do not replace medically managed withdrawal or prescribing care.

interventions.title: Eating-disorder multidisciplinary coordination
interventions.try: An appropriately trained clinician helps coordinate medical/nutritional monitoring, family or support involvement with consent, and individualized psychological care within scope.
interventions.measure: Review medical status with the team and patient-centered participation; avoid relying on body size alone.
interventions.scope: Medical instability and refeeding decisions require qualified specialist oversight.

interventions.title: Specialist eating-disorder cognitive work
interventions.try: Within coordinated care, assess rules, fear, self-evaluation, access needs and maintaining context. Use a collaboratively selected treatment model without prescribing restriction or numeric intake goals here.
interventions.measure: Review functioning, psychological flexibility and medically reviewed progress.
interventions.scope: Not a self-help exposure or refeeding protocol.

interventions.title: Specialist binge/purge pattern formulation
interventions.try: With qualified care, map contextual triggers, cycles, compensatory behavior and physical risk. Select coordinated evidence-based treatment components and ensure medical review.
interventions.measure: Monitor frequency and harm, functioning, and agreed clinical indicators without shaming.
interventions.scope: Electrolyte and other medical risks require appropriate assessment.

interventions.title: Therapist-supported eating-rule flexibility
interventions.try: Explore rigid rules and shame in a consented, specialist setting; co-design safer behavior-change work coordinated with nutritional/medical care.
interventions.measure: Monitor reduced impairment and sustainable participation, with medical outcomes interpreted by the team.

interventions.title: Multidisciplinary feeding access formulation
interventions.try: Distinguish sensory, fear, appetite, swallowing, nutritional and environmental contributors with appropriate specialist assessment; adapt context and meal access with consent.
interventions.measure: Review nutritional/medical stability, tolerable participation and accommodation effectiveness.
interventions.scope: Do not prescribe unmonitored food exposures or assume no medical risk.

interventions.title: Clinician-led graded food participation
interventions.try: Qualified clinicians, with appropriate medical/nutritional clearance, collaboratively structure noncoercive, paced food-participation work and adjust to sensory/communication needs.
interventions.measure: Track choice, functional eating participation and medical safety as assessed by the team.
interventions.scope: No pressure, forced intake or substitution for indicated medical evaluation.

interventions.title: CBT-I sleep-pattern formulation
interventions.try: A qualified clinician reviews a structured sleep diary, daytime functioning, medications and relevant medical causes; identifies an appropriate treatment component and checks safety.
interventions.measure: Measure sleep patterns alongside daytime participation and unwanted effects.
interventions.scope: Sleep restriction is not a generic self-help exercise; screen for bipolar, seizure and other relevant risks.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided sleep environment review
interventions.try: Assess noise, light, pain, caregiving demands, neurodivergent needs and routines with the person; prioritize realistic modifications and review impact.
interventions.measure: Compare sleep continuity and daytime fatigue across feasible changes.

interventions.title: Integrated symptom-and-care formulation
interventions.try: Validate the reported symptoms and suffering, review indicated medical care, stress and attention patterns without prematurely psychologizing, and coordinate a shared care plan.
interventions.measure: Measure functional burden, care access and quality of life as well as symptom distress.
interventions.scope: Do not use symptom response to rule out disease or delay appropriate investigation.

interventions.title: Collaborative medical communication session
interventions.try: Help the person prepare questions and a coherent account of symptoms and functional impact; with consent coordinate expectations among treating clinicians.
interventions.measure: Track whether medically indicated follow-up occurred and whether the person felt heard and could function.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided pacing and participation design
interventions.try: Differentiate flare patterns, medical guidance, accessible effort and valued activities. Collaboratively build flexible pacing based on sustainable participation instead of mandatory pushing.
interventions.measure: Track chosen activities, recovery time, flare impact and burden of the plan.

interventions.title: Pain-related threat and coping formulation
interventions.try: In session examine perceived threat, lived constraints, uncertainty, avoidance and supports without dismissing pain as psychological. Integrate with appropriate medical treatment.
interventions.measure: Measure function, agency, pain interference and whether the person's concerns receive appropriate care.

interventions.title: Cognitive-access and environment consultation
interventions.try: With the person and appropriate supports, evaluate memory, comprehension, wayfinding and functional safety; trial simpler cues and adaptations to daily routines.
interventions.measure: Track successful chosen tasks with supports and caregiver burden rather than unaided performance alone.

interventions.title: Supported communication and care planning
interventions.try: Facilitate accessible discussion of preferences, goals, roles and future supports, accounting for decision-specific ability, communication needs and consent.
interventions.measure: Review whether choices are expressed and honored, participation preserved and supports realistically available.
